page: Microsoft Azure HB176-144rs_v4 is a member of the HBv4 server family, built on the x86_64 architecture with an Intel processor. This virtualized instance runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor and features 144 dedicated vCPUs. It is equipped with 768.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 5.33 GB of RAM per core. The server includes 4332 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and supports Premium Storage configurations.

The instance is RDMA capable, enabling low-latency, high-throughput interconnectivity for clustered environments. It does not feature any GPU hardware, meaning workloads requiring hardware acceleration must rely entirely on the CPU. Additionally, the server does not include any complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Given its high core count, dedicated CPU allocation, and substantial local NVMe storage, this server represents a high-density resource profile. The inclusion of RDMA capability makes it suitable for tightly coupled high-performance computing workloads, large-scale simulations, and computational fluid dynamics. The 4332 GB NVMe SSD also supports data-intensive processing, database hosting, and storage-heavy operations that benefit from high-speed local scratch space.
